entry_points.name: delete_account
entry_points.note: HTTP route gallery/<int:pk>/delete/ calls delete() on the Account row.

entry_points.name: admin.site.register
entry_points.note: Registering Account in the Django admin gives both admin_delete_model, the single-object delete view, and admin_delete_selected, the bulk action, as ways to delete an account row.

stores.name: gallery_account

erasure.note: The delete_account view calls delete() on the Account instance, which removes the row.

stores.note: Table holding the account holder record.

stores.name: gallery_photo

fields.name: caption
fields.note: Free-text field filled in by the account holder.

erasure.note: The foreign key to Account uses on_delete=models.CASCADE, so deleting the account removes the photo rows.

stores.note: Table of photos, one account holder per row through the account foreign key.

stores.name: gallery_comment

fields.name: body
fields.note: Text column the account holder writes into.

erasure.note: The foreign key to Account uses on_delete=models.CASCADE, so deleting the account removes the comment rows.

stores.note: Table of comments, tied to an account holder through the account foreign key.

stores.name: photo.image

fields.name: image
fields.note: Image file uploaded by the account holder under the prefix photo/images/; the schema does not constrain what it shows.

erasure.note: The only receiver that deletes a stored file is registered for the sender Comment, and Comment has no image field, so deleting the Photo row leaves the uploaded file on storage; django_cleanup is not installed.

stores.note: Uploaded image files written under the upload_to prefix photo/images/.
